chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Her first vaudeville engagements
summary: Her first vaudeville engagements at Loew's State and the variety acts on the bill.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: first engagements at the vaudeville house at the Loews State. I went in with my arrangements. I had maybe about eight or nine songs and I thought I was going to get a chance to sing them all and the manager would come back and say, you got twelve minutes. So I had to pick out three or four good tunes. That's the advantage or disadvantage of working vaudeville. You only need about four arrangements. And you do these over and over again. Of course, one of the problems I ran into, some of the pit bands, the instrumentation wasn't the same as I had so I wound up having to transfer parts almost everywhere I went. And of course when I went to; I toured Great Britain in 1948 and again in 1953. I was over there and I really had to shuffle my arrangements around because every band had a different instrumentation in the pit. They used mostly pit bands then. I wasn't traveling - at that time there just wasn't that many bands. In London proper they had a Palladium which featured big bands. But they had their own band there which played alot of the American swing arrangements. But the other houses, they're called the variety houses, they would have a pit band and they would have different types of
